html:
The siege of Rhodes was a year-long attack on the island city of Rhodes in 305 and 304 BCE by Demetrius, son of Antigonus the One-Eyed, one of the generals fighting over Alexander's empire. It failed, and it became one of the most famous sieges of the ancient world.

Rhodes was a rich trading city that tried to stay neutral in the wars of the successors, but it was close to Ptolemaic Egypt, its main grain partner. Demetrius came to force it to change sides. He brought a huge army and fleet and some of the largest siege engines ever built, among them the Helepolis, "city taker", a giant armoured tower on wheels full of catapults.

The Rhodians fought back hard, and Ptolemy sent supplies. After a year Demetrius gave up and made a deal: Rhodes would stay independent and help his father except against Ptolemy. Demetrius still earned the name Poliorcetes, "the Besieger".

He left his siege machines behind. The Rhodians sold them and used the money to build the Colossus of Rhodes.
